Vendored repository size and redundancy review

Source: VENDOR_REVIEW.md

Date: 2026-10-25. This is a review; no repository files were removed, moved, rewritten, or repacked.

Findings

The two local reference checkouts total 3.281 GiB in logical file sizes. 1.917 GiB is in their Git stores; the checked-out files total 1.364 GiB.

Checkout Working files (MiB) Git store (MiB) Total (MiB)
MLV_toolbox/ 712.18 1240.01 1952.18
vendor/pyMLV/ 684.92 722.89 1407.81

Both are complete, non-shallow Git clones. The MATLAB checkout has 459 commits reachable from HEAD; Python has 16. Their tracked and untracked status checks were clean. Their exact revisions and origins are recorded in VENDOR_DUPLICATES.json.

The largest individual files are the pack files: approximately 1,239.27 MiB for MATLAB and 722.77 MiB for Python. They hold Git objects for the checkouts and their histories; they are not disposable cache files. Deleting a pack file would damage its repository.

The MATLAB checkout is currently at MLV_toolbox/; Python is at vendor/pyMLV/. These are the paths actually inspected.

Confirmed duplicates

SHA-256 checks of same-size regular-file candidates at least 1 MiB found 33 exact duplicate groups, representing 661.04 MiB of repeated logical working-tree data. All copies have distinct file identities; none are existing hard links.

Repeated material Duplicate groups One-copy reduction (MiB) Assessment
All dataset MAT files across both repositories 30 650.54 Strongest consolidation candidate: retain one complete shared dataset copy
demos/Forest_DBW.mat across both repositories 1 7.74 Keep one historical reference copy and preserve provenance
images/example_output.png and images/medial_axis_transform.png 2 2.76 Repeated illustrations; small savings
Python MLVcode/MAT.mat versus demos/MAT.mat 1 payload match 7.78 Full hashes differ, but all bytes after their 128-byte MATLAB-v5 headers match

The dataset duplication includes IAPS, OASIS, TorontoScenes, ArchitecturalScenes, and Snodgrass/Vanderwart. This conclusion comes from checksums, not just matching names or sizes. The largest pair is dataSets/TorontoScenes/cities_vecLD.mat, at 41.87 MiB per copy.

The two Python MAT.mat files are each 8,160,320 bytes. Their complete-file SHA-256 values differ, but both have MATLAB-v5 headers and the payload SHA-256 is identical: 683382d03752b8b7259ab34f7203dec7a4f51df726c0c57c637c67ee045898ac. Thus header differences explain why ordinary full-file checksums did not group them. The code explicitly writes MAT.mat from computeMAT(); retain at least one copy until its provenance and regeneration behavior are documented.

Keeping one instance of every confirmed exact/payload duplicate would reduce logical working-tree content by about 668.82 MiB. Removing tracked paths from a checkout does not remove their existing objects from Git packs.

The exact-duplicate scan was limited to files at least 1 MiB. Smaller repeated documentation, source assets and metadata were not exhaustively checksum-tested.

Additional material to slim or exclude

Material Observed size Role and recommendation
MATLAB MLVcode/edges-master/ 33.99 MiB Legacy structured-edge backend, including a trained forest model and a large bundled toolbox. Defer from a minimal analysis snapshot; preserve as an optional backend reference
MATLAB demos/ 21.54 MiB Mix of useful inputs, live scripts and generated figures; keep scripts/inputs selectively after identifying dependencies
Python demos/ 19.96 MiB Includes the repeated MAT/Forest artifacts and notebooks; retain notebooks as code references
Python notebook embedded outputs About 4.38 MiB serialized Almost all notebook bulk is saved output/images; clear outputs in a derived snapshot, retaining original inputs and cells
Python docs/ and MATLAB doc/ 1.69 + 0.53 MiB Generated documentation; optional in a compact vendor tree
MATLAB resources/ 0.24 MiB MATLAB project metadata; low-value storage reduction

Python’s contour-feature notebook is 3.77 MiB and the medial-axis notebook is 0.63 MiB. Their serialized output records occupy approximately 4.38 MiB combined; this is an estimate from JSON serialization rather than a measured output-cleared file-size difference.

The first-party MATLAB MLVcode/*.m source is about 0.16 MiB, and the Python code is similarly small once embedded MAT artifacts are excluded. Most disk usage is reference data, object stores and bundled dependencies.

Do not classify every MAT file as redundant. For example, vendor/pyMLV/MLVcode/imgLD.mat is a distinct raster input, and Python’s README says the medial-axis demo currently depends on MATLAB-rendered input. The demonstration forest MAT file also preserves a historical processed result; regeneration from the current source has not been established.

Recommended cleanup design

  1. Keep one shared reference-data collection. Consolidate the repeated dataset files and Forest example using the checksum manifest. Record the canonical destination and the source repositories/commits for each retained item. Update reference harness paths before removing any duplicate copy. Avoid writable hard links between independently editable checkouts.

  2. Vendor pinned source snapshots for the R port. Preserve the exact commit, origin, licenses and required helper files in a source manifest. Export only the needed code/reference artifacts into the eventual compact layout. If full Git history is still wanted locally, a shared Git object store or separately retained clone is another option. Shallow/sparse clones can help, but their actual footprint must be measured; neither guarantees removal of all large current-tree blobs.

  3. Keep expensive or historical fixtures selectively. Retain one copy of the MAT payload, useful rendered input, tiny synthetic fixtures and selected demonstrations. Preserve original specimens until replacements are independently reproducible. Keep legacy RGB weights/backends separate from ordinary contour-analysis development.

  4. Exclude local references from R distribution. Once package scaffolding exists, use explicit build exclusions for the vendor checkouts, reference data, object stores and model weights. Confirm the tarball contents. Exclusion affects packaging; it does not reclaim local disk space.

A compact source-only snapshot could remove most of the current checkout footprint from the working project, while one shared dataset copy remains available for optional scientific evaluation. Exact final savings require a staged replacement, verification of its needed files and data, and a decision about custody of the full clones. The 1.917 GiB Git-store total is not a promise that a history-preserving cleanup can recover that amount.

Verification and limitations

  • Read every regular file’s metadata inside the two scoped checkouts; no permission errors or symlinks were encountered.
  • Hashed 68 candidate files, totaling about 1337.64 MiB of I/O, and checked file size/modification time before and after hashing.
  • Examined source references and notebook output sizes without displaying image or dataset contents. No MAT datasets were loaded into the model or a scientific analysis.
  • Recorded Git heads, remotes, shallow status, commit counts, object-store summaries and clean worktree status.
  • Filesystem allocated-block totals are approximately 3.295 GiB, but APFS shared/cloned extents mean sums of file sizes or allocated blocks do not establish uniquely reclaimable space.
  • The volume reported approximately 20 GiB available during review.
  • No deletion, history rewrite, clone conversion, notebook clearing, source change, or data relocation was performed.
